heading: Image Compressor Online for Smaller Image Files
introduction:
Use this tool to make JPG, JPEG, PNG and WebP images smaller. Choose a quality mode, compare the original and new sizes, and download the result.
An image compressor helps reduce the amount of data stored in an image file. This makes photographs and graphics easier to manage while allowing you to maintain suitable visual quality for their intended use.

File Compresser provides a free online image compressor for JPG, JPEG, PNG and WebP images. You can select images from your device, choose a suitable quality mode and compare the original file with the processed version. The tool works directly in your browser, so your selected images are not uploaded to the website's servers.

sections.heading: What Is an Image Compressor?
sections.body:
An image compressor is a tool that reduces an image's file size by changing how its data is stored. Depending on the image format and selected method, it may remove unnecessary information, adjust image quality or reduce the number of colors.

The purpose is to create a file that is easier to upload, download, store or display online. File Compresser supports several common image formats, each with different characteristics.

sections.heading: JPG and JPEG Images
sections.body: JPG and JPEG are widely used for photographs. They are suitable for product pictures, personal photographs, travel images and many website graphics. The compression process uses quality settings to balance file size and visible detail. Lower quality settings can produce smaller files, but they may also create visible artifacts around edges, textures and small text.

sections.heading: PNG Images
sections.body: PNG is commonly used for logos, screenshots, diagrams and graphics that need transparent backgrounds. Unlike JPG, PNG can preserve transparency. File Compresser provides separate PNG modes, including Lossless, Smart, Maximum and Target size. The selected mode determines whether decoded pixels are preserved or colors may be reduced to create a smaller file.

sections.heading: WebP Images
sections.body: WebP is an image format designed for web use. It supports lossy and lossless compression, as well as transparency. It can be useful for website photographs and graphics where smaller downloads are important. However, an existing WebP image may already be optimized, so further compression does not always create a smaller result.

sections.heading: How to Compress Images Online
sections.body:
You can use File Compresser without installing an image editing application. The process involves selecting your images, choosing settings and reviewing the output.

Open the Image Compressor page.
Select JPG, JPEG, PNG or WebP images from your device.
Wait for the website to validate the selected files.
Choose a suitable compression mode.
Enable resizing only if you need different image dimensions.
Start processing.
Compare the original and final image sizes.
Inspect the image quality and download the result.

The original image dimensions are maintained by default. If you enable resizing, the aspect ratio is preserved and smaller images are not enlarged.

sections.heading: Choose the Right Compression Mode
sections.body: Selecting the right quality mode is important because different images have different requirements.

sections.heading: Maximum
sections.body: Maximum is the default mode for the general image compressor. It applies a stronger compression trade-off to reduce file size. For JPEG and WebP, this can affect visible image detail.

sections.heading: Balanced
sections.body: Balanced offers a more moderate approach. It is useful when you want to reduce file size without choosing the strongest compression setting.

sections.heading: High Quality
sections.body: High Quality prioritizes more visual detail. The output may be larger than a result created with a stronger compression setting.

sections.heading: PNG Lossless
sections.body: PNG Lossless preserves decoded image pixels. It is a suitable option when exact pixel appearance matters more than achieving the smallest possible file.

sections.heading: Target Size
sections.body: Target Size attempts to create an image within a specified maximum file size. It checks the actual output bytes rather than simply estimating the result. If the requested size cannot be achieved, the tool reports that the target was not met.

sections.heading: Why Should You Compress Images for Websites?
sections.body:
Large images are one of the common reasons web pages contain heavy resources. When a website uses unnecessarily large photographs, visitors may need to download more data than required for the displayed image. Optimizing images can help reduce page weight and make website resources easier to load.

For website owners, image compression is useful for:

Product photographs on online stores.
Featured images in blog articles.
Homepage banners and promotional graphics.
Team photographs and business profiles.
Screenshots and tutorial images.
Portfolio and project galleries.

Image compression is only one part of website optimization. Dimensions, responsive image delivery, caching and other page resources also affect loading performance.

sections.heading: Should You Resize an Image Before Compressing It?
sections.body:
Compression and resizing are two different operations. Compression changes how image information is stored. Resizing changes the actual pixel dimensions of an image.
For example, a large photograph may have more pixels than a website section needs. Reducing its dimensions can remove unnecessary image data and may provide a larger size reduction than compression alone.

However, resizing is not always necessary. If you need to preserve the original dimensions, keep the resize option disabled. File Compresser does not silently resize images. You can enable resizing when a smaller width or height is required.
